## fast-glob.diff.we-reject-UnterminatedBrace
# A `{` that never closes (7 rows)
# An unclosed `{` is a parse error (GLOB_SPEC §6.4); the library keeps the
# brace as literal text.
# fast-glob: no-match  [tests/test.rs:1728]  (and 1 more path)

## fast-glob.diff.we-reject-UnterminatedClass
# A `[` that never closes (6 rows)
# globstar reads classes by POSIX's rules (GLOB_SPEC §8.5): a `]` first in the
# list is literal, and a class cannot hold `/`, so a `[` with no closing `]`
# after that is a parse error. The library accepts the pattern, as literal
# text or with the class crossing `/`; its answer is the row's comment.
# fast-glob: no-match  [tests/test.rs:50]
\\/$^+?.()=!|{},[].*	\/$^+?.()=!|{},[].*	err:UnterminatedClass
# fast-glob: no-match  [tests/test.rs:710]
foo[/]bar	foo/bar	err:UnterminatedClass
# fast-glob: no-match  [tests/test.rs:717]
[/]	/	err:UnterminatedClass
# fast-glob: no-match  [tests/test.rs:1825]
src/[abpp.js	src/app.js	err:UnterminatedClass
# fast-glob: no-match  [tests/test.rs:1826]  (and 1 more path)
!src/[abpp.js	src/app.js	err:UnterminatedClass

## fast-glob.diff.brace-degenerate
# A brace with one branch (3 rows)
# A brace needs two branches to be a brace (GLOB_SPEC §6.1): `{a}` and `{}`
# are literal text here, and the library expands them.
# fast-glob: match  [tests/test.rs:1718]
{}{},	,	no-match
# fast-glob: match  [tests/test.rs:1719]
{}{}}	}	no-match
# fast-glob: match  [tests/test.rs:1720]
{a,{b,c}}{},	b,	no-match

## fast-glob.diff.we-reject-TrailingBackslash
# A pattern ending in `\` (3 rows)
# A `\` at the end escapes nothing and is refused (GLOB_SPEC §4.1); the
# library drops it or keeps it as a literal backslash.
# fast-glob: no-match  [tests/test.rs:1827]
src/app.js\	src/app.js	err:TrailingBackslash
# fast-glob: no-match  [tests/test.rs:1828]
!src/app.js\	src/app.js	err:TrailingBackslash
# fast-glob: no-match  [tests/test.rs:1836]
!abc\	xyz	err:TrailingBackslash

## fast-glob.diff.backslash
# A backslash in the pattern (1 row)
# `\X` is the literal `X` for every `X` (GLOB_SPEC §4.1), inside classes too,
# and a path is never unescaped. The library gives some escapes another
# meaning (`\b`, `\w`), keeps the backslash, or unescapes the path.
# fast-glob: no-match  [tests/test.rs:597]
a[\b]c	abc	match
